Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Money, work & business · Conversation, family & daily routines

pocket money noun

also allowance, spending money, pocket-money

classical

Liv. 2.41.10: pecūliumque fīliī, and the son’s own money
Plaut. Asin. 498: nec potest pecūlium ēnumerārī (Lewis & Short)

pecūlium, pecūliī n.

noun, second declension

a child’s own money: pocket money

What a Roman father let his son, or a master his slave, hold and spend as his own (Lewis & Short); also his savings (see save, money).

Examples

  • quā rē velim cūrēs (nec tibi essem molestus, sī per alium hoc agere possem) ut permūtētur Athēnās quod sit in annuum sūmptum eī

    so please see to it (I would not trouble you if I could do it through anyone else) that his allowance for the year is sent to Athens by bill of exchangeCic. Att. 15.15.4

  • Ecce tibi pecūlium; nummōs in loculōs dēmitte.

    Here’s your pocket money; drop the coins in your money box.composed

Other words

  • sūmptus, sūmptūs m. — spending money, an allowance

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 15.15.4: quod sit in annuum sūmptum eī, what he needs for his year’s allowance; Cic. Att. 12.32.2

    Cicero’s word for his son’s allowance as a student at Athens; properly expense (see spend, money).

See also save, money, coin, wallet, spend.

SourcesLewis & Short: peculium · Lewis & Short: sumptus
